A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ZILOT research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results across 30 tasks in five environments, including baseline comparisons, ablations, single-goal evaluations and qualitative trajectories.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Forward-Backward baseline evaluations, training curves and analyses of the training-data distribution.

M1.justification: ZILOT retains the same learned dynamics model, state-goal and goal-goal value functions, Sinkhorn objective, finite-horizon planning and goal-conditioned TD-MPC2 implementation. The newly described Forward-Backward adaptations concern comparison methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 30 tasks across three Fetch environments, HalfCheetah and PointMaze, with the same WGCSL, curiosity-collected and D4RL datasets. Single-goal evaluation already appears in v1; the new coverage analysis examines existing data and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ERFB and RERFB to the retained Pi+Cls and MPC+Cls comparisons, introducing a distinct Forward-Backward method family. The single-goal comparison also adds these methods and the three ZILOT ablations, expanding from three to eight methods.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained. The added FB comparisons introduce a two-million-step training budget, evaluation every 50,000 steps and best-checkpoint selection (Appendices C.10 and D.2). Appendix C.8 adds selection of the five closest training trajectories for coverage analysis.

E4.justification: Appendix C.8 adds dataset-support and nearest-trajectory analyses addressing whether demonstrations reproduce training trajectories. Appendix D.2 adds FB training-length sensitivity curves, and the single-goal study gains ablation controls. The original component, horizon and classifier-threshold analyses remain.

E5.justification: The 20-trial, five-seed mean and standard-deviation reporting and Welch tests at p=0.05 are unchanged. Appendix C.8 newly introduces kernel density estimation of training goal occupancies, a limited addition of statistical estimation rather than increased runs or new uncertainty tests.

E6.justification: All retained numerical entries in Tables 1 and 2 are unchanged. v2 adds extensive FB results, expanded single-goal results, training curves, coverage findings and baseline timing. For example, Fetch Slide aggregate Wmin is newly 0.250/0.251 for ERFB/RERFB versus retained ZILOT 0.098; on HalfCheetah backflip, both new baselines achieve 2.002 versus ZILOT 2.625.

T1.justification: The myopia proposition, its proof and ZILOT derivations are unchanged. Appendix B adds formal definitions of the FB reward objectives, including the expert-to-data density ratio and its regularized counterpart. This is limited mathematical elaboration, without a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims remain offline, zero-shot imitation from one rough, partial demonstration through occupancy matching, with reduced myopia. The clearer terminology and additional comparisons support the existing contribution without redefining its scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for FB performance involving limited data and degenerate reward-maximizing solutions. It interprets unseen trajectories as combinations of states within training-data support and discusses ZILOT's non-Markovian policy space. The existing limitation from world-model accuracy and finite horizons is retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.10 and Table 8 document FB implementation adaptations, goal inputs, normalization, representation sizes, learning rates, batch sizes and discounts. Appendix C.3 adds matched-hardware MPC+Cls timing of 12–35 Hz alongside ZILOT's retained 0.5–3 Hz. Original ZILOT settings and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 recognizes Forward-Backward methods as an exception to v1's broad statement about zero-shot RL and distribution matching. New Appendix B extensively positions ZILOT against Pirotta et al. (2024), explaining applicable and excluded variants. Jeen et al. and additional reward-based imitation references are also added.

P1.justification: Most original prose and the main argument sequence remain intact. v2 clarifies rough versus partial demonstrations, renames Conclusion to Discussion, shortens selected passages and reorganizes the appendices, including moving the qualitative gallery after the hyperparameter searches.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch to two columns. Table 1 moves into the appendix and gains FB columns; baseline, density and training-curve displays are added. Figure 4 removes the Pi+Cls panel, ablation plots are restyled, and retained trajectory galleries are redistributed across pages.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important comparison gap by evaluating a distinct, closely related FB method family and documenting its adaptation and checkpoint selection. The training-data analyses better substantiate what unseen-trajectory imitation demonstrates, while runtime and limitations discussions expose practical costs. These additions substantially strengthen the empirical case, although conclusions about FB remain specific to the adapted, limited-data setting.
